content: Agent Grid is now in public preview, bringing identity-based Zero Trust network security to AI agents on supported Azure environments. Security teams can govern communications among agents, models, tools, and external services through centrally managed policies. Enforcement operates outside the agent’s trust boundary, without agent code changes or customer-managed sidecars. Preview capabilities include TLS inspection, fully qualified domain name (FQDN) filtering, URL filtering, granular Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool filtering, and Azure Content Safety integration for Prompt Shields. Administrators can allow specific tools on an approved MCP server while blocking sensitive operations, restrict outbound destinations, and inspect supported content for prompt-injection attacks. Agent Grid applies common policies across onboarded ACI Agent Groups, AKS Agent Sandbox using Kata Containers, and native Kubernetes workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). Verified workload identities, mutually authenticated encrypted connectivity, and centralized enforcement visibility help security teams protect agent workflows across supported hosting environments. Learn more: Documentation Announcement blog
